I will start from what has worked on my land and then adjust where the money is worth spending. I have 10.1 mu, and with well water I do not need to farm defensively like a dryland household. I have been doing this a long time, so I look at each crop by yield target, fertilizer response, and cash return. Chili is my main money crop, so I will put the best land and more fertilizer there, especially nitrogen and potassium, because if chili is short of肥 it shows fast in plant vigor and fruit setting. Wheat and maize are steadier crops for me, and I will manage them more by balance: enough fertilizer to protect yield, but not so much that I waste cash. I do not like cutting fertilizer too close. If I am uncertain, I would rather leave a little extra in the field than lose production. On my farm size, 10.1 mu, I can still manage carefully by myself and with family labor, but I also need a plan that is simple enough to execute on time. So this year I will keep most area in chili, and I will keep wheat and maize on smaller blocks with rates I know can hold yield under irrigated conditions in Quzhou.
